newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down as anniversary rally flops.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down as anniversary rally flops.

text.p: Taiwan stocks on Tuesday defied expectations for a government-orchestrated rally to celebrate the first anniversary of President Lee Teng-hui's inauguration, losing more than one percent at the close.

The weighted index see-sawed in a narrow range after a slightly higher opening, but heavy selling pressure emerged in the final 30 minutes to drag the index lower. The index ended down 110.79 points or 1.37 percent to 7996.75.
Turnover was a weak T$66 billion.
"Investors were very disappointed after seeing the stock market fail to meet widespread expectations of a so-called May 20 celebration rally," said Jardine Fleming fund manager George Hou.

Investors and analysts had speculated that state-related funds, conglomerates and institutions would orchestrate a price rally to mark completion of Lee's first full year as the first democratically elected president in Chinese history.
Market watchdogs had denied that such state intervention was in the works, despite Taiwan's long record of politically inspired "celebration rallies".
Brokers said they had detected no obvious intervention.
"Certain government-related institutions might have entered in late trade to prevent a big plunge, but they were quite low-key," Jardine's Hou said.
Electronic shares led Tuesday's decline, tumbling 2.21 percent as a sector. Blue chip Taiwan Semiconductor was down T$3 or 2.88 percent to T$101.

Financials, a regular target for political buying due to their heavy weighting and big state holdings, fell 2.02 percent on brisk selling. Hua Nan Bank, one of the "big three" state-run banks, lost T$4 or 3.33 percent T$116.
